summary: In-gun Kang works in Buddhist and religious studies. Kang studied at the Jesuit School of Theology, the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under multiple teachers, and earned a doctorate at Heythrop College under Michael Barnes.

Ines Konczak specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She held a postdoctoral fellowship at Staatliche Museen zu Berlin and was a visiting research fellow at Ryukoku University in 2012.

Ingmar Heise specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. Heise completed an MA in Chinese studies at Leiden University in 2005 and was attested as a PhD candidate at the University of Bristol in 2012.

Ingo Strauch is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from the Free University of Berlin in 2000. He taught Kathrin Holz and is attested as a professor at the University of Lausanne in 2018.
Inyoung Chung is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at the University of Virginia under the supervision of Paul Groner, attested in 2008.

Isabelle Henrion-Dourcy specializes in Tibetology. She studied at Free University of Brussels, Harvard University, EPHE, and Tibet University, and taught anthropology at Laval University circa 2004 and 2007.
Isabelle Onians is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She received her PhD from the University of Oxford in 2002 and has served as an editor for the Clay Sanskrit Library.

Isabelle Ratié specializes in Indology and philosophy. Educated at Paris 1 and EPHE, she held posts at Paris, the Austrian Academy of Sciences, Leipzig, and Sorbonne Nouvelle (2014–2025) before joining the Collège de France in 2025.

Isaline Blew Horner was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Newnham College (ca. 1914–1917). She served the Pali Text Society from ca. 1936 to 1981, as Honorary Secretary (ca. 1942–1958) and President (ca. 1959–1981).

Iselin Frydenlund works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. In 2016, she was attested as a senior researcher at the Peace Research Institute Oslo and a research fellow at the University of Oslo.

Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. After studying at Sanskrit Collegiate School and Sanskrit College and University, he served as director of Sanskrit College and University from circa 1851 to 1858.
Issaen Ikeyama was a Buddhist studies scholar who held professorships at Shitennoji Junior College and Eizan Gakuin, both attested in 1976.
Issei Suzuki was a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Rissho University and subsequently served as a professor there.
Issei Yamakawa is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his education at Sophia University and Aichi Gakuin University, where he undertook a master's program.

Ivan Minayev was an Indologist and linguist who studied at St. Petersburg State University and under Albrecht Weber. He served as a professor at St. Petersburg State University from circa 1871 to 1890.

Ives Waldo is a scholar of philosophy, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Oxford, studied under Chögyam Trungpa between 1970 and 1988, and taught David P. Jackson.

Ivette Vargas-O'Bryan specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from Harvard University in 2003 under Leonard van der Kuijp and held a fellowship at Grinnell College.

Ivo Fišer was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He served as a lecturer at Charles University, attested in 1960, and held a post at the University of Copenhagen's Institute for Indian Philology, attested in 1970.

Iwao Nakajima studied under Nichiki Kimura and earned a master's degree at Hitotsubashi University. He worked at the NHK Broadcasting Culture Research Institute (ca. 1958–1975) and served as chief editor at Sandhaan (attested 1999).

Iwao Shima was a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. After studying at Nagoya University (ca. 1969–1978), he worked at Kanazawa University from circa 1984 to 2007, serving as professor from circa 1996 to 2007.
